subjectLine: Zero-Days Dominate: Windows BitLocker Bypass, Cisco SD-WAN Exploited, AI-Powered 2FA Attacks

articles.title: Windows Zero-Days Expose BitLocker Bypass and Privilege Escalation
articles.summary: Two new Windows zero-day vulnerabilities have been disclosed, one allowing for a BitLocker bypass and the other enabling privilege escalation via the CTFMON component. These critical flaws, codenamed YellowKey and GreenPlasma, pose a significant threat to Windows system security.

articles.title: Zero-Day Exploit Defeats Windows 11 BitLocker Protections
articles.summary: A critical zero-day exploit has been discovered that completely bypasses the default BitLocker encryption protections on Windows 11. Microsoft is investigating this severe vulnerability, which could allow attackers to access encrypted data without authorization.

articles.title: AI Used to Develop First Known Zero-Day 2FA Bypass for Mass Exploitation
articles.summary: Google has disclosed the first known instance of a zero-day exploit, likely developed using AI, to bypass two-factor authentication (2FA). This marks a significant escalation in cybercrime capabilities, demonstrating AI's potential for creating sophisticated exploits for widespread attacks.

articles.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller Authentication Bypass Actively Exploited
articles.summary: Cisco has released updates to address a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-20182) in its Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, which has a CVSS score of 10.0. The flaw has reportedly been exploited in limited attacks, allowing attackers to gain administrative access to the network manageme

articles.title: Cisco SD-WAN Flaw Exploited in Zero-Day Attacks
articles.summary: Cisco is alerting users to a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in its Catalyst SD-WAN Controller that has been actively exploited in zero-day attacks. The flaw allows attackers to gain administrative privileges on compromised devices.

articles.title: Maximum Severity Cisco SD-WAN Bug Exploited in the Wild
articles.summary: A critical Cisco SD-WAN vulnerability with a CVSS score of 10.0 is being actively exploited by threat actors in the wild. This marks the second time this year a severe flaw in Cisco's network control system has been leveraged, emphasizing the need for rapid patching of high-impact network infrastruc

articles.title: CISA Adds Cisco SD-WAN Authentication Bypass to KEV Catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-20182) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Federal agencies are mandated to patch this issue by May 17, 2026, due to its potential for administrative access exploitation.

articles.title: Pwn2Own Berlin: Zero-Days in Windows 11, Exchange, and RHEL Demonstrated
articles.summary: During Pwn2Own Berlin 2026, competitors successfully exploited 15 unique zero-day vulnerabilities, earning significant cash awards. Exploits targeted major software including Windows 11, Microsoft Exchange, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux, demonstrating critical security flaws in widely used platforms.

articles.title: Windows 'MiniPlasma' Zero-Day Exploit Grants SYSTEM Access
articles.summary: A new zero-day vulnerability in Windows, dubbed 'MiniPlasma,' has been publicly disclosed with a proof-of-concept exploit. This vulnerability allows attackers to escalate privileges to SYSTEM level on fully patched systems. The release of a PoC significantly increases the risk of widespread exploita

articles.title: 18-Year-Old NGINX Rewrite Module Flaw Enables Unauthenticated RCE
articles.summary: A critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-42945) in the NGINX rewrite module, undetected for 18 years, has been disclosed. This flaw allows for unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE), posing a severe risk to web applications relying on NGINX.

articles.title: 18-Year-Old NGINX Vulnerability Allows DoS and Potential RCE
articles.summary: A long-standing vulnerability in the NGINX web server, dating back 18 years, has been discovered and can be exploited for denial of service and potentially remote code execution. This critical flaw underscores the importance of regularly auditing and patching even mature software components.

articles.title: Russian APT Turla Enhances Kazuar Backdoor for Persistent P2P Botnet Operations
articles.summary: The Russian state-sponsored hacking group Turla has evolved its Kazuar backdoor into a modular peer-to-peer botnet designed for stealth and persistent access. articles.title: Russian Hackers Evolve Kazuar Backdoor into Modular P2P Botnet
articles.summary: The Russian state-sponsored hacking group Secret Blizzard has transformed its long-standing Kazuar backdoor into a sophisticated modular peer-to-peer (P2P) botnet. articles.title: Critical Linux Kernel Vulnerability 'Copy.Fail' Disclosed
articles.summary: A severe Linux kernel vulnerability, dubbed 'Copy.Fail' (CVE-2026-31431), has been disclosed, allowing local privilege escalation. The exploit abuses the kernel crypto API and splice() functionality to write data directly into a file's page cache, posing a significant risk.

articles.title: New Fragnesia Linux Kernel LPE Grants Root Access via Page Cache Corruption
articles.summary: A new Linux kernel local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerability, dubbed Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300), allows attackers to gain root access by corrupting the page cache. This marks the third such critical kernel vulnerability discovered in two weeks, highlighting ongoing issues with Linux kernel secu

articles.title: Linux Kernel Dirty Frag LPE Exploit Grants Root Access
articles.summary: A new unpatched local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerability in the Linux kernel, dubbed Dirty Frag, allows attackers to gain root access. This exploit is considered a successor to the Copy Fail vulnerability and poses a widespread risk to major Linux distributions.

articles.title: New 'Dirty Frag' Exploit Threatens Enterprise Linux Distributions
articles.summary: A newly discovered privilege escalation vulnerability, named 'Dirty Frag,' poses a significant risk to enterprise Linux distributions. Similar to previous flaws like Copy Fail and Dirty Pipe, this exploit may already be under limited exploitation, potentially impacting many systems.

articles.title: Microsoft Warns of Exploited Exchange Server Zero-Day Flaw
articles.summary: Microsoft has issued a warning about a critical zero-day vulnerability in Exchange Server that is actively being exploited. The flaw allows attackers to execute arbitrary code via cross-site scripting (XSS) targeting Outlook on the web users.

articles.title: Exploited Vulnerability in On-Premise Microsoft Exchange Server
articles.summary: Microsoft has confirmed active exploitation of a spoofing vulnerability (CVE-2026-42897) in on-premise versions of Exchange Server. This cross-site scripting flaw, with a CVSS score of 8.1, poses a significant risk to organizations still managing their own Exchange infrastructure.

articles.title: Ghostwriter Targets Ukrainian Government with Geofenced PDF Phishing
articles.summary: The Belarus-aligned threat group Ghostwriter has launched new attacks against Ukrainian government entities using geofenced PDF phishing campaigns. This operation, linked to cyber espionage and influence operations, highlights the ongoing geopolitical cyber warfare impacting Eastern Europe.

articles.title: 'FrostyNeighbor' APT Targets Government Orgs in Poland and Ukraine
articles.summary: The nation-state threat group 'FrostyNeighbor,' believed to be linked to Belarus, is conducting targeted espionage campaigns against government organizations in Poland and Ukraine. articles.title: Azerbaijani Energy Firm Hit by Chinese Nation-State Actors
articles.summary: An unnamed Azerbaijani oil and gas company was targeted in a multi-wave intrusion by a Chinese-affiliated threat actor known as FamousSparrow. This incident highlights the ongoing targeting of critical energy infrastructure by nation-state actors for espionage purposes.

articles.title: China's 'FamousSparrow' APT Nests in South Caucasus Energy Firm
articles.summary: The China-linked advanced persistent threat (APT) group 'FamousSparrow' has been observed repeatedly targeting an energy firm in the South Caucasus. This expansion of targeting beyond traditional sectors like hospitality and government highlights the evolving strategies of nation-state actors.

articles.title: Mini Shai-Hulud Worm Compromises Major AI and Dev Packages
articles.summary: The threat actor TeamPCP is behind a new Mini Shai-Hulud campaign that has compromised popular npm and PyPI packages from companies like Mistral AI and Guardrails AI. The compromised packages contain obfuscated JavaScript designed to profile the execution environment.

articles.title: TeamPCP Compromises Checkmarx Jenkins AST Plugin, Weeks After KICS Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary: Checkmarx has confirmed that a modified version of its Jenkins AST plugin was compromised and published to the Jenkins Marketplace by threat actor TeamPCP. articles.title: cPanel CVE-2026-41940 Actively Exploited to Deploy Filemanager Backdoor
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in cPanel and WebHost Manager (WHM), tracked as CVE-2026-41940, is being actively exploited by threat actor Mr_Rot13 to deploy the Filemanager backdoor. This authentication bypass flaw allows remote attackers to gain elevated control over compromised hosting environments.

articles.title: Exploited WordPress Plugin Flaw Steals Payment Data from WooCommerce Checkouts

articles.title: PraisonAI Authentication Bypass Vulnerability Exploited Within Hours of Disclosure
articles.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-44338) in the PraisonAI framework was actively exploited by threat actors just four hours after its public disclosure. articles.title: AI Hallucinations Pose Real Security Risks to Critical Infrastructure
articles.summary: AI hallucinations, where models generate confident but incorrect outputs, are creating significant security risks, particularly in critical infrastructure decision-making. articles.title: Attackers Leverage AI and LLMs for Exploit Development and Automation
articles.summary: Cyber adversaries are increasingly using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) to develop sophisticated exploits and automate complex attack campaigns. This trend signifies a new era in cyber warfare, where AI-powered tools enhance attacker capabilities.

articles.title: OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Matches Mythos AI in Vulnerability Discovery
articles.summary: The UK's AI Security Institute has found that OpenAI's GPT-5.5 is as effective as Anthropic's Mythos AI in discovering security vulnerabilities. Notably, GPT-5.5 is generally available, making its advanced vulnerability detection capabilities accessible to a wider audience.

articles.title: DigiCert Mishap Exposes Critical Infrastructure, Microsoft Responds
articles.summary: A significant security incident involving DigiCert briefly compromised trust in millions of Windows systems due to a support error, leading to a heavy-handed response from Microsoft. articles.summary: NIST's National Vulnerability Database (NVD) has changed its enrichment policy, now covering only a fraction of CVEs. articles.title: TanStack Supply Chain Attack Affects OpenAI Employee Devices
articles.summary: OpenAI has reported that two employee devices were compromised through a supply chain attack targeting the TanStack software. articles.title: Microsoft Patches 138 Vulnerabilities, Including Critical DNS and Netlogon Flaws
articles.summary: Microsoft has released patches for 138 security vulnerabilities across its product range, with 30 rated as critical. While none are publicly known or under active attack, the update addresses significant issues including privilege escalation bugs and critical flaws in DNS and Netlogon services.
